questions.question: Identify the importance of group cohesion in group dynamics. (,U)
questions.solution_html:
• Strengths
  •  Identifies group relationships: Helps understand patterns of attraction, rejection, and interaction among members
  •  Detects group structure: Reveals leaders, isolates, cliques, and sub-groups within the group
  •  Improves group functioning: Assists the worker in planning interventions to enhance cohesion and participation
  •  Visual representation: Sociograms provide a clear and simple diagram of complex relationships
  •  Useful for decision-making: Helps in forming balanced groups and assigning roles effectively
  • Limitations
  •  Risk of labeling: Members may feel stigmatized as “isolates” or “rejected”
  •  Depends on honesty: Accuracy relies on truthful responses from members
  •  Time-consuming process: Data collection and diagramming require effort and skill
  •  Static in nature: Captures relationships at one point; may not reflect changing dynamics
  •  Ethical concerns: Issues of confidentiality and misuse of sensitive interpersonal data
  • Conclusion
  • Sociometry and sociograms are powerful tools for understanding group dynamics, but they must be used carefully and
  • ethically to avoid harm and ensure accurate interpretation.
questions.source_exam: Official Model Question Paper (FYUGP 2024
questions.final_answer: Strengths

questions.question: Assess the strengths and limitations of Sociometry and Sociograms in professional group work practice.
questions.solution_html:
• Strengths
  •  Identifies group relationships: Helps understand patterns of attraction, rejection, and interaction among members
  •  Detects group structure: Reveals leaders, isolates, cliques, and sub-groups within the group
  •  Improves group functioning: Assists the worker in planning interventions to enhance cohesion and participation
  •  Visual representation: Sociograms provide a clear and simple diagram of complex relationships
  •  Useful for decision-making: Helps in forming balanced groups and assigning roles effectively
  • Limitations
  •  Risk of labeling: Members may feel stigmatized as “isolates” or “rejected”
  •  Depends on honesty: Accuracy relies on truthful responses from members
  •  Time-consuming process: Data collection and diagramming require effort and skill
  •  Static in nature: Captures relationships at one point; may not reflect changing dynamics
  •  Ethical concerns: Issues of confidentiality and misuse of sensitive interpersonal data
  • Conclusion
  • Sociometry and sociograms are powerful tools for understanding group dynamics, but they must be used carefully and
  • ethically to avoid harm and ensure accurate interpretation.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
questions.final_answer: Strengths
